g.text: An infographic overview of geography, economy, demographics, and travel.
Map shows the four largest cities by metropolitan population.

<tspan x="610" dy="0">Japan, known as Nihon or Nippon, is an island nation in East</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">Asia. Located in the Pacific Ocean, it lies to the east of the Sea of</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">Japan, China, and Russia. Its geography is characterized by rugged</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">mountains, dense forests, and a long coastline. The country is</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">renowned for its seamless blend of ancient traditions and cutting-</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">edge technology.</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="35">The four largest cities—Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka, and Nagoya—</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">are situated on the main island of Honshu and serve as the</tspan> <tspan x="610" dy="20">primary hubs for commerce, culture, and population.</tspan>

<tspan x="90" dy="0">Despite facing demographic challenges with an aging population, Japan remains a global economic powerhouse. It is a leader in automotive, electronics, and robotics</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">industries. The nation's cultural heritage—ranging from the tea ceremony and classical architecture to modern anime and cuisine—continues to captivate people</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">worldwide. Visitors are drawn to its vibrant metropolises, serene shrines, and stunning seasonal landscapes.</tspan>

<tspan x="90" dy="0">Japan holds the position of the world's fourth-largest economy by</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">nominal GDP. The chart illustrates the trajectory of Japan's</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">nominal GDP from 2015 to 2024 in current US dollars.</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="35">While the economy peaked in 2019 at $5.12T, recent years have</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">seen a contraction, largely influenced by yen depreciation and</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">global economic fluctuations.</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="35">The 2022–2024 period shows a noticeable dip below the $4.5T</tspan> <tspan x="90" dy="20">mark, highlighting the macroeconomic challenges facing the nation.</tspan>
Note: Small slices exaggerated visually via thick stroke for readability.
The bustling capital, blending ultramodern neon streets with ancient temples.
The cultural heart of Japan, home to thousands of classical temples and shrines.
A vibrant food hub known for its lively street food scene and nightlife.
Historic city of peace and the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima.
The majestic sacred peak of Japan, surrounded by hot springs and scenic views.
The northernmost island, famous for snowy winters, nature, and fresh seafood.
Data sources: World Bank, IMF, Statistics Bureau of Japan. Figures are nominal and in current US$.
